walkthroughs.body_html:
Density & Pressure — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Density & Pressure brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Density & Pressure.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A 200 g block has volume 100 cm³. Its density is:
options: 0.5 g/cm³
2 g/cm³
20 g/cm³
200 g/cm³

mcqs.q: An object will float in water if:
options: it is light
its mass is less than water's mass
its density is less than water's
it is hollow

mcqs.q: Why does increasing the intensity of light below the threshold frequency not eject electrons?
options: Enough low-frequency photons should eventually eject an electron if you wait long enough.
The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.
Low-frequency light doesn't have enough mass to push electrons out of the metal.
Each photon's energy is below the work function; many low-energy photons can't combine to eject an electron.

mcqs.q: Is the cosmological redshift of distant galaxies a true Doppler shift?
options: Yes — it is the same Doppler shift as a moving siren on Earth.
No — it arises from the expansion of space stretching photon wavelengths during transit, not from the galaxy's motion through space.
No — it is caused by dust in space absorbing blue light.
Low-frequency light doesn't have enough mass to push electrons out of the metal.
